title: The Agentic Marketing Department
subtitle: A multi-agent AI system that covers the jobs of a small marketing team — content, social, analytics, and iteration.

tiles: Specialist AI agents for strategy, copy, visuals, social, and analytics
Agents hand off through Make.com scenarios — no human ferrying tasks
Analytics agent feeds results back into the strategy agent
Self-improving loop: performance data tunes the next campaign
challenge: A real marketing department has a strategist, a copywriter, a designer, a social manager, and an analytics lead — five salaries minimum. Small businesses need the same breadth of output but can't staff it, and stringing together point AI tools just hands the coordination problem back to the owner. The real challenge was making the coordination itself automatic: getting specialized agents to hand off cleanly and learn from each other.
approach: I designed a multi-agent system where each function lives in its own LLM-backed agent with a defined role: one plans the content calendar, one writes copy, one briefs visuals, one schedules social posts, and one reads performance data back from the platforms. Make.com (a visual automation layer) orchestrates the handoffs — the analytics agent's output feeds the strategy agent's next brief, which creates a self-improving loop instead of a one-shot generation. Every agent has guardrails on tone, brand, and escalation back to a human when it isn't sure.
result: The system autonomously runs the core work of a small marketing department — calendars, social publishing, campaign reporting, and creative iteration — at a fraction of the headcount cost. Performance improves over time without manual tuning because analytics feeds back into strategy. This is the clearest demonstration in my portfolio that AI agents can collapse departmental coordination, not just individual tasks.
